reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure, every complete real inner-product normed space H, every map F:E->H and assignment D:E->(E->L[R]H), assume F has full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at every w:E. Let M1,M2 be supplied nonnegative real numbers, with norm_op(D(w))<=M1 for every norm_E(w)<=1, and norm_op(D(w)-D(u))<=M2*norm_E(w-u) for every w,u in the closed unit ball. Fix any y:H. Use the following literal definitions. Let S={w:E | norm_E(w)=1}, with its inherited topology and measurable structure, and write w_bar for the ambient representative of w:S. Set K(w)=F(w_bar) and c(w,u)=arccos(inner_product_E(w_bar,u_bar)). For every measure mu on S define m(mu)=integral_S K(w) dmu(w) in H. For mu:Measure S and ambient w:E set V(mu,w)=2*inner_product_H(m(mu)-y,F(w)), and G(mu,w)=2 times ((D(w)).adjoint(m(mu)-y)-inner_product_E((D(w)).adjoint(m(mu)-y),w) times w). Define Q(mu,nu) as the infimum in the nonnegative extended reals of integral_lower_{S times S} ofReal(c(w,u)^2) dgamma(w,u), over all actual product-space measures gamma whose first pushforward marginal is mu and second is nu. Here integral_lower is the nonnegative extended Lebesgue integral. The empty feasible infimum is infinity, and no optimizer is selected or asserted. The map ofReal takes the nonnegative part, and the vector mean is the actual Bochner integral, totalized to zero if it is not genuinely integrable. Then all the following hold: There exist real C1>0 and C2>0, fixed for all the following laws and points. For every probability mu on S, K is genuinely Bochner integrable under mu; for every ambient w:E, V(mu,.) has gradient 2 times (D(w)).adjoint(m(mu)-y) at w; and for every unit-subtype point w:S, inner_product_E(w_bar,G(mu,w_bar))=0 and norm_E(G(mu,w_bar))<=C1. For every probability pair mu,nu on S, Q(mu,nu)!=infinity and for every w,u:S, norm_E(G(mu,w_bar)-G(nu,u_bar))<=C2*((Q(mu,nu)^(1/2)).toReal+c(w,u)). HasGradientAt means that the full real Frechet derivative in any direction v is inner_product_E(2 times (D(w)).adjoint(m(mu)-y),v)=2*inner_product_H(m(mu)-y,D(w)(v)). Mu is fixed when taking that derivative, and the ambient point w is not restricted to the unit ball in this gradient conclusion. For norm_E(w)=1, G(mu,w) is the orthogonal projection of this ambient gradient onto the subspace perpendicular to w. It is that projected vector which receives the uniform norm and transport-plus-angle estimates; the statement does not substitute G for the full ambient gradient. The means are defined for arbitrary laws by the totalized integral formula, but the stated integrability and estimates are conditional on the laws being probabilities. No feature integrability or finiteness of Q is supplied as a hypothesis: those are conclusions. Q is the actual squared-angular-cost infimum. Its explicit finiteness makes its extended square root finite, so toReal is the ordinary nonnegative real value and not its special value zero at infinity. No positive lower bound on Q is assumed. The final estimate compares two arbitrary probability laws and two exact unit points with the same C2; it is not restricted to finite support. The constants may depend on the fixed E,H,F,D,M1,M2,y but not on mu,nu,w,u. They are strictly positive without an asserted formula or sharpness, while the supplied M1,M2 are only nonnegative. No positive-dimensionality or nonempty-unit-set premise appears; if S is empty the probability-conditioned clauses are vacuous, while the existence of positive C1,C2 is still asserted. The concrete angular cost and infimum definitions do not assert a new metric/geodesic API or an attained optimal coupling, and no derivative with respect to the law variable is stated.
objects: Finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E with its Borel measurable structure; complete real inner-product normed space H; supplied F and its full derivative assignment D; supplied nonnegative M1,M2; fixed y:H; unit subtype S; restricted feature K; actual angular scalar cost c; actual Bochner mean m; scalar V; projected formula G; extended squared-cost coupling infimum Q; and uniform positive output constants C1,C2.

K:S->H, c:S times S->R, m:Measure S->H, V:Measure S->E->R, G:Measure S->E->E, Q:Measure S->Measure S->nonnegative_extended_reals. Mu,nu are arbitrary measures in the definitions, with probability premises in conclusions. Unit points w,u in estimates are subtype points; ambient w in the gradient clause ranges over all E.
quantifiers: For every E,H and their stated structures, F,D, a supplied proof of HasFDerivAt(F,D(w),w) for every w, nonnegative M1,M2 satisfying the two uniform closed-ball operator estimates, and fixed y, let S,K,c,m,V,G,Q have the exact formulas. The second block quantifies every pair mu,nu with both probability, asserts finite Q, and then the single C2 bound for every w,u:S. Constants are not chosen separately per law or point.

Laws in the respective universal clauses must be probabilities. K integrability, gradient representation, tangent orthogonality, positive output constants, finite transport infimum and the final estimates are generated conclusions rather than assumptions. No pointwise feature bound, finite support, optimizer, metric axioms for an arbitrary cost, or law-variable differentiability hypothesis is supplied.

scopes: The first gradient representation is full ambient differentiation of the explicit scalar function V(mu,.) with mu fixed and valid at every ambient w, including outside the unit ball. Its gradient is the unprojected vector 2*(D(w)).adjoint(m(mu)-y). G has the given algebraic formula on all ambient points; at unit points it subtracts exactly the normal component, so the orthogonality and norm bounds concern the tangent projection, not a claim that G is the full ambient gradient. Input bounds on D use the closed unit ball, whereas projected-vector estimates use exact unit points. The mean is a genuine Bochner integral for each probability law by an explicit integrability conclusion; outside that analytic scope its definition retains totalized-zero semantics if nonintegrable. Q uses the nonnegative extended integral of ofReal(c^2) over actual couplings with ordered marginals, not a signed or truncated measure difference. Its finiteness is explicit; therefore the displayed square-root toReal has its ordinary finite value. The angular argument is literal arccos of unit representatives, and no arbitrary metric, geodesic identification, or minimizing-coupling API result is asserted. All parameter probabilities, including nonatomic laws, fall within the stated conditions. Empty S is permitted. There is no law derivative, scalar risk definition, or additional loss functional among the conclusions.
constant_dependencies: M1,M2 are supplied nonnegative operator-norm bound and Lipschitz constants on the radius-1 closed ball. C1,C2 are existential strictly positive reals depending at most on the fixed E,H,F,D,M1,M2,y, uniform over all probability mu,nu and all unit points w,u. The packet specifies no formula, minimality, dimension independence, or independence from the feature offset or y. V and the projected formula G have literal coefficient 2. The cost is exactly c squared, with exponent 1/2 applied to the extended infimum and no extra factor. The joint estimate has one common coefficient C2 multiplying the sum of the finite root transport value and c(w,u); there is no particle count or additional normalization denominator.
